title: Way to Specialist: Closing Loop Between Specialized LLM and Evolving Domain Knowledge Graph

problem.claim: Generalist LLMs fall short on reasoning tasks requiring specialized knowledge.

gap.claim: Existing specialization approaches require substantial domain-data acquisition and model fine-tuning efforts.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes the Way-to-Specialist framework, combining retrieval-augmented generation with knowledge graphs to improve specialized LLM capability without specialized training.
The LLM↻KG paradigm enables bidirectional enhancement between a specialized LLM and a domain knowledge graph.
WTS couples DKG-Augmented LLM retrieval and prompting with LLM-Assisted DKG Evolution that generates new domain knowledge from processed tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validation on 7 datasets spanning 6 domains.
The authors report that WTS surpasses the previous state of the art in 5 specialized domains.
The authors report a maximum performance improvement of 11.3%.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs perform strongly across many domains.
Generalist LLMs remain weak on specialized-knowledge reasoning tasks, while prior specialization methods require substantial data acquisition and fine-tuning.
WTS combines retrieval-augmented generation with knowledge graphs through bidirectional interaction between a specialized LLM and an evolving domain knowledge graph.
The framework closes the loop so the system can progressively answer domain-specific questions and learn from them.
The authors report evaluation across multiple datasets and domains, with state-of-the-art results in five specialized domains and a maximum improvement of 11.3%.

source_observation.claim: The framework couples task-time retrieval and reasoning with feedback that evolves the domain knowledge graph.

interpretation.claim: A knowledge source can become more useful when system outputs and processed tasks contribute structured updates back to it.

application.claim: For specialized question-answering systems, consider a controlled loop in which task processing informs incremental domain-knowledge updates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how generated knowledge is validated or how harmful or incorrect updates are prevented.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental settings in detail.
The abstract does not specify the knowledge-update validation process or error-control mechanisms.
